artifacts.summary: Rules on /approve's placement (new extension, not books/core), the interaction design reconciling the AskUserQuestion option cap with step-through UX, the MEASURED/INFERENCE confidence vocabulary, and the specs/certificates/ naming convention, grounded in the now-completed Verification companion task and the task-300 AskUserQuestion rehome pattern.

memory_candidates.content: When AskUserQuestion must run from a direct-execution skill (never a dispatched agent, per task 300's settled unreachability finding), reconcile a 'many items, one cheap decision' UX against AskUserQuestion's 4-option-per-question cap by composing two existing precedents: (1) an option-availability-gated bulk triage question first (email extension's bulk-bucket-review.md: an unsafe bulk option simply does not exist as a choice rather than being offered then filtered, using a MEASURED not impressionistic gate), then (2) a per-item step-through loop with exactly 4 options (Approve/Decline/Discuss this item/Decide later). A 'discuss/open files' escape does not need a dedicated menu option when the skill runs in the root session and the artifact is persisted at a predictable path -- the owner can detour into conversation or open the file directly at any time, independent of the pending question.

This repository already has a two-tier, non-impressionistic confidence vocabulary precedent worth reusing whenever a task needs to label a claim's certainty: MEASURED (a mechanically verified fact, e.g. digest/cone-walk equality) vs INFERENCE (a completeness or judgment claim the tooling does not independently check), from Logos/Verification's books/convention/09-trust-unit-is-the-export.md (Decision 9) and BookCert/Depends.lean. Prefer citing/deriving from this precedent over inventing a graded or numeric confidence scale.

For a no-task-number-keyed persisted artifact, this repository's existing precedent is /review's specs/reviews/review-{DATE}.md (with an observed -{suffix} disambiguator, e.g. review-2026-09-22-roadmap.md) -- a date-based identity, not an empty/placeholder task segment. Combine with artifact-formats.md's zero-padded MM_ sequence-number convention for the instance axis when both a task-keyed and a no-task-keyed form must coexist under one naming scheme.
